value.rationale: The sticky wall represents reversible trapping at a boundary, with the escape outlet at the opposite end. The exact threshold distinguishes when very weak full-state restarting reduces versus increases mean escape and moves in a monotone, measurable way with stickiness. The singular strong-trapping result demonstrates that positive-rate resets from any strictly interior location rescue an otherwise divergent escape time, while resetting on the trap cannot help. This nonuniform reset-location boundary is a substantive and experimentally relevant control consequence beyond a routine zero-stickiness moment calculation.
